subsystem_notes.note: Pervasive pattern: vendor drivers consume the base _snmp_get/_snmp_walk results (which silently return None / {} on any SNMP error) without guards, so regex/.startswith/indexing on SNMP-derived values crash during exactly the reboot/transient-loss windows these methods poll through; firmware/config setters compound this by returning True without verifying the SET echo.

Discovery walkers are mostly termination-safe (is_new_mac/is_new_ip guards + bounded ARP fallback), but the new-device gate has a short-circuit ordering bug that silently drops shared-IP devices and poisons their MAC; the LLDP parser and parsers.py make format/key assumptions that crash or silently lose neighbours on partial SNMP/lldpctl responses; the DHCP management-network match is a dotless prefix; and ospf.generate_entries is a silent no-op that never emits the per-device routes its own docstring promises.

Two systemic defect classes dominate: (1) number_coaches() BFS variants that re-enqueue devices keyed only on coach_number (no visited set) — DostoNeuReport can loop forever on unmatched topology; (2) pervasive use of SNMP-derived fields (config/firmware/serial) and get_device() results without None-guards, causing NoneType crashes across device.py, dani, via, ace, dsb, ccjpa_wd2, rules_engine. GenericReport/TGV/TGV2020/Luna/Daisy/CCJPA-wd1 are comparatively well-guarded.

FastAPI action/consist routers; the actions router imports HTTPException from the wrong module (http.client, not fastapi), which turns every intended 404/405 into a runtime TypeError that is either masked as success or surfaced as a 500, and togglepoe dereferences an instantiate_device result that can be None.

Tree build is the weak point: an unresolved neighbour MAC and a None/empty root both crash the whole update before any device is touched. Leaf-first ordering itself (calculate_parallel_update_order on a shallow tree copy) is correct, and the BFS terminates via the `mac not in tree` guard. The dominant defects are None-derefs in the tree build and in needs_*_update, plus the empty-device-set silent no-op via all([])==True.

Backbone CLI commands are riddled with TODO stubs and missing-guard control flow; the two strongest defects are handle_ssid continuing after a failed report load (None-deref) and a hardcoded "Waffles" SSID stub that silently reconfigures every AP. Validation/zabbix paths trust SNMP-derived fields that can be None. Config singleton and disk cache are mostly sound.

confirmed.title: VDSRail firmware-update polling crashes on SNMP failure (None.search)
confirmed.claim: re.search("Not running", result) raises TypeError when result is None because _snmp_get returns None on any SNMP error.
confirmed.trigger: During set_firmware_version, the switch drops/ times out the snmp_firmware_task_running_oid GET (reboot window, transient loss, wrong OID) so _snmp_get returns None.
confirmed.repro: Call VDSRailDevice.set_firmware_version(target) on a switch that stops answering SNMP after the update trigger; line 71 result=None, line 74 re.search(pattern, None) -> 'TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object'. Loops every 1s for up to 120s, each iteration re-crashing on the first None.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading the actual code. vdsrail.py:71-74 does `result = self._snmp_get(self.device_config["snmp_firmware_task_running_oid"])` then `search = re.search("Not running", result)` with NO None-check between. snmpdevice.py:324-340 shows `_snmp_get` returns `result.get(oid)` (dict .get -> None when key absent). snmpdevice.py:283-322 (`_snmp_parse_results`) shows that on `error_indication or error_status` (SNMP timeout, no-response, wrong OID) the loop does `continue`, leaving the result dict empty, so `_snmp_get` returns None on any SNMP failure — the hunter's premise is statically true. `re.search(pattern, None)` raises `TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object`. The `result = ""` init at line 68 is overwritten at line 71 before the regex, so it gives no protection. No upstream guard prevents the trigger: the only caller (update.py:205-214) wraps the call in `try/except SNMPDeviceException`, and SNMPDeviceException is `class SNMPDeviceException(Exception)` (snmpdevice.py:56) which TypeError does NOT subclass — so the TypeError propagates uncaught. Same identical bug pattern also exists in set_configuration_version (line 116), confirming it is the intended-but-broken idiom, not a typo. Marked confirmed (not needs_runtime_confirmation) because the None can be produced by the code itself and the crash on None is statically guaranteed; the SNMP timeout that yields None during a firmware reboot window is an ordinary operating condition, not exotic hardware-specific data.
verdict.covered_by_test: None found. tests/lib/device/vendor/test_vdsrail.py only covers test_reboot and test_neighbours; there is NO test for set_firmware_version or the None-result path. The SNMPMock._snmp_get (lines 44-45) does a strict dict lookup that would raise KeyError, not return None, so it does not model SNMP-failure behavior at all.
verdict.blast_radius: VDSRail vendor only (VDSRailDevice.set_firmware_version), i.e. the `obn update f` firmware-push path for VDS Rail consist switches — DOSTO/Stadler fleet. Does not affect the 14 report variants or other SNMP vendors (each vendor has its own set_firmware_version). The twin bug at vdsrail.py:116 extends the same exposure to `obn update c` config pushes on the same switches. Per project notes the fleet currently sits at target fw 7.4.2 so most pushes are no-ops, narrowing real-world hit rate, but any actual firmware push to a switch that times out SNMP in the reboot window crashes the updater for that device.

confirmed.title: VDSRail set_firmware_version/set_configuration_version/reboot return True without verifying success
confirmed.claim: These methods return True unconditionally (TODO comment admits it), so a failed SNMP SET / failed reboot is reported as a successful firmware/config push.
confirmed.trigger: Any SNMP SET in the sequence is silently dropped (e.g. factory-config switch ignoring writes, or reboot OID not honoured) but the prior poll loop happened to see 'Not running'.
confirmed.repro: On a switch that accepts the GET poll but silently ignores the set_default / reboot SETs (_snmp_set swallows errors and returns {}), set_firmware_version still returns True at line 96; reboot() returns True at line 131 even though _snmp_set never set the reboot OID. Caller marks the device updated when nothing changed.

verdict.reasoning: Read vdsrail.py:57-131. set_firmware_version ends `self.reboot(); return True  # TODO: return True only on successful call` (line 95-96); set_configuration_version ends identically (line 124-125); reboot() does two `_snmp_set` calls then `return True  # TODO` (line 129-131) with NO read of the SET result. _snmp_set (snmpdevice.py:392-426) delegates to _snmp_parse_results (lines 283-322), which on `error_indication or error_status` logs and `continue`s, returning {} — it never raises and never propagates failure. So a silently-dropped SNMP SET (factory switch ignoring writes, unhonoured reboot OID) cannot turn the return False. The firmware path has ONE partial guard: the 120s poll loop (lines 69-93) returns False on timeout / unexpected task string, but a dropped set_default/reboot SET after a successful 'Not running' poll still returns True. set_configuration_version and reboot have zero post-SET verification. The sole consumer, cli/update.py update_device (lines 205-219), does not even read the boolean — it calls the method in a try/except (only catching SNMPDeviceException, which _snmp_set never raises) and then unconditionally pprints 'firmware/configuration update applied, device rebooting.' So a no-op push is always reported as applied. The TODO comment is an explicit admission.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/lib/device/vendor/test_vdsrail.py::TestVDSRail::test_reboot exists but does NOT refute — it mocks _snmp_set (so a failed SET is impossible to observe) and asserts only `mock_set.call_count == 2`, never the return value or any success verification. No test exercises set_firmware_version or set_configuration_version for VDSRail at all. No green test contradicts the claim.
verdict.blast_radius: All VDSRail consist switches (DOSTO/Stadler) for `obn update f`/`obn update c`/reboot via cli/update.py and the /reset_device API route (actions.py:46 returns this unverified True as `success`). The same `return True # TODO` pattern is replicated in lantech.py:67, tng4500.py:76, westermo.py:83, so the no-verify anti-pattern spans multiple vendors; the CLI caller ignoring the return value affects every vendor's update path equally.

confirmed.title: ACKSYS _load_file raises the device class instead of an exception
confirmed.claim: raise AcksysDevice(...) raises the AccessPointDevice subclass (not AcksysException) with positional args its __init__ does not accept, producing a TypeError that masks the intended config/file error message; same bug at lines 424 and 453.
confirmed.trigger: snmp_firmware_instructions / snmp_config_instructions missing from vendors YAML (line 419), the firmware/config file not on disk (line 423), or the upload-init SNMP SET returning falsy (line 452).
confirmed.repro: Call set_firmware_version with a config_key absent from device_config; line 420 executes 'raise AcksysDevice("device config is missing %s config", config_key)'; AcksysDevice.__init__ expects (mac, ip, ccu_interface, brand) so this raises a confusing TypeError/argument error instead of the intended descriptive AcksysException.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at src/usr/share/obn/lib/device/vendor/acksys.py. Line 420: `raise AcksysDevice("device config is missing %s config", config_key)`; line 424: `raise AcksysDevice("file does not exist: %s", file_path)`; line 453: `raise AcksysDevice("failed to initialise ACKSYS SNMP upload")`. `AcksysDevice` (defined line 48) is `class AcksysDevice(AccessPointDevice)`; the inheritance chain is AccessPointDevice (accesspointdevice.py:8) -> SNMPDevice (snmpdevice.py:99) -> Device (device.py:11) which is `class Device(ABC)` — NOT a BaseException subclass. Therefore `raise AcksysDevice(...)` cannot raise the intended descriptive error: Python evaluates the expression then rejects it with `TypeError: exceptions must derive from BaseException` (and the positional args `mac="device config is missing %s config", ip=config_key` are fed into the full Device SNMP-backed construction chain, which can throw an unrelated error first). Either way the intended message is masked. This is unambiguously a bug because every other raise in the same file uses the proper exception class AcksysException (defined line 26 as `class AcksysException(Exception)` with `__init__(self, message)`): lines 206, 313, 482, 495, 527, 560, 562 — including lines 482/495 inside this very `_load_file` function. The three AcksysDevice raises are the only anomalies. No upstream guard prevents the trigger; the `if config is None` (419), `if not os.path.isfile(file_path)` (423), and `if not result` (452) checks ARE the branches that fire the buggy raise. Note the claim's secondary assertion about arity is imprecise: AcksysDevice.__init__ accepts 4 positional params (mac, ip, ccu_interface, brand), so 2 positional args is valid arity — the TypeError comes from raising a non-BaseException, not from an argument-count mismatch. The error-masking outcome stands regardless.
verdict.covered_by_test: None found for the defect path. tests/lib/device/vendor/test_acksys.py has test_set_firmware_version (line 125) and test_set_configuration_version (line 132) — the only tests reaching _load_file — but both are @pytest.mark.skip("needs physical hardware") (lines 124, 131) and never exercise the error branches. The two green `with pytest.raises(AcksysException)` tests (lines 345, 404) cover get_connected_devices / get_connected_devices_list, a different method, and assert the correct AcksysException — they do not touch _load_file.
verdict.blast_radius: ACKSYS vendor only, on the AP firmware/config SNMP upload path (set_firmware_version / set_configuration_version -> _load_file). Fires only on a genuine error precondition: missing snmp_firmware_instructions/snmp_config_instructions key in vendors YAML, firmware/config file absent on disk, or upload-init SNMP SET returning falsy. Not the DOSTO fleet's primary AP vendor (Westermo/Eltec/Extreme dominate); does not affect the 14 report variants or non-ACKSYS SNMP devices. Impact is degraded diagnostics (confusing TypeError instead of a clear cause) on an already-failing ACKSYS upload, not a functional regression of a working path.

confirmed.title: DostoNeuReport.number_coaches() unconditional re-enqueue with no visited set → infinite loop
confirmed.claim: A neighbour that passes the None/coach-number guard is appended to the queue at line 158 unconditionally even when no numbering branch set its coach_number, so two mutually-connected devices that never get numbered ping-pong forever.
confirmed.trigger: Any cabling/discovery state where a SW or AP neighbour relationship matches none of the if/elif branches (lines 65-155) so coach_number stays None, and that device has an unnumbered neighbour back to it.
confirmed.repro: Discovery JSON: BOX (numbered) -> SWa on port 6 (not LAN1/LAN2 -> coach_number stays None) and SWa <-> SWb mutually listed as neighbours but on ports that match no SW-SW branch. number_coaches pops SWa, enqueues SWb (coach None), pops SWb, enqueues SWa, ... loop never terminates; memory/CPU blow-up (mirrors the report-OOM seen in the field).

verdict.reasoning: Read report_dosto_neu.py:31-163 (whole number_coaches), device.py (Device.coach_number defaults to None, line 23), and report.py get_device (401-404). The cited line 158 `queue.appendleft(to_device)` runs UNCONDITIONALLY for every neighbour that clears the guard at line 61 (`if to_device is None or to_device.coach_number is not None: continue`). That guard is the ONLY re-enqueue protection — there is no visited/seen set and no iteration cap (grep of report.py for visited/seen/max_iter returned nothing). The numbering branches at 65-155 are all conditional on device_number/coach_number/port; if a neighbour relationship matches none of them, coach_number stays None (the branch fell through without assignment), yet line 158 still enqueues the device. So two mutually-listed neighbours (LLDP neighbour lists are mutual; get_device resolves by MAC) that both stay None ping-pong: pop SWa -> SWb still None -> appendleft(SWb); pop SWb -> SWa still None -> appendleft(SWa); forever. The line-61 guard never fires for them because neither ever gets a coach_number. Statically the loop is unavoidable given such input. The 'continue' at line 159 is a no-op (last statement in the for-body). Marked confirmed rather than needs_runtime_confirmation because the control-flow defect is fully provable from the source and the field has already observed the matching report-OOM loop, though the specific malformed-cabling discovery JSON is the actual trigger.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/lib/report/test_report_dosto_neu.py::TestDostoNeuReport::test_number_coaches — exercises number_coaches() but ONLY with well-formed discovery fixtures (discovery_nv4_2_coaches.json, discovery_nv6.prev.json, discovery_fv5.json, discovery_fv6.json) where every neighbour matches a numbering branch. None contains two mutually-connected unnumbered devices, so the green test neither covers nor contradicts the defect; it asserts correct numbering on correct cabling only.
verdict.blast_radius: DOSTO-NEU report only (DostoNeuReport.number_coaches); the other 13 report variants do not share this method. Within DOSTO it affects all train_types routed here (nv4/nv6/fv5/fv6). Entry point is `obn report`, which hangs and grows the queue unbounded (CPU/memory blow-up) when fed malformed cabling/discovery data.

confirmed.title: VIAReport.number_coaches() references box_device before assignment when no CCU box found
confirmed.claim: box_device is only bound inside the loop when a BOX with matching serial is found (line 31-37); if no such device exists (serial None or no box), line 144 self.find_neighbour(box_device, ...) raises NameError (UnboundLocalError).
confirmed.trigger: CCU SNMP serial returns None, or no BOX device whose serial startswith the ccu device id, so the assignment at line 37 never runs.
confirmed.repro: Run VIAReport on discovery JSON where the CCU's serial is None -> 'box_device' is referenced at line 144 before assignment -> UnboundLocalError, report aborts.

verdict.reasoning: In src/usr/share/obn/lib/report/report_via.py, VIAReport.number_coaches() declares box_device only at line 37 (box_device = dev), inside the conditional `if dev.type == "BOX" and dev.serial and dev.serial.startswith(self.get_ccu_device_id())` (lines 30-34) within the loop over self.device_instances.values(). After the loop, line 144 reads it unconditionally: `master_switch = self.find_neighbour(box_device, lambda x: x.get("port") == 1)`, and line 155 reads it again (parsed_devices.add(box_device.mac)). There is no post-loop guard (no `if box_device is None: return`, no try/except, no default `box_device = None` before the loop). If the loop never enters the line-30 block — because no device has type=="BOX" with a truthy serial that startswith the ccu device id — box_device is never bound and line 144 raises UnboundLocalError (a NameError subclass), aborting the report run inside Report.report() at report.py:624. The None-check inside find_neighbour (report.py:408 `if device is None`) does NOT rescue this: box_device is UNBOUND, not None, so the exception fires at the argument-read on line 144 before find_neighbour is even called. Device.serial defaults to None (device.py:10), and the function's own comments (report_via.py:41-43) explicitly anticipate devices that 'failed to respond to SNMP or SSH queries', so a CCU box with a None/missing serial — or a mismatched ccu_box_id — is a realistic input. I grepped the whole obn tree for box_device: it is a pure local in report_via.py (assignment at :37, reads at :144 and :155) with no instance/class attribute fallback. The unguarded reference is statically provable; classifying as confirmed since it is a definite code defect, though firing it requires discovery data with no matching BOX device.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/lib/report/test_report_via.py (TestVIAReport.test_via_report and test_via_report_missing_neighbours) — both ALWAYS set configuration["ccu_box_id"] to a value (box1-t1 / box1-t8) that matches a BOX device with a real serial in the discovery fixtures, so box_device is bound in every parametrization. No test exercises the no-matching-BOX / serial-None path, so no green test covers or contradicts the defect.
verdict.blast_radius: Single report variant: VIAReport only (VIA = hybrid-consist customer; report_module "VIAReport" per tests/test_backbone_discovery.py:67). DOSTO/ÖBB trains use report_dosto_neu.py / report_generic, which have their own number_coaches() and are unaffected. Each of the other 13 report variants has an independent number_coaches() implementation. Triggers per-run during VIA consist reporting whenever the CCU box device fails to present a serial matching get_ccu_device_id() (SNMP/SSH failure on the box, None serial, or misconfigured ccu_box_id) — aborts that train's report generation/MQTT publish.

confirmed.title: actions.py imports HTTPException from http.client, not fastapi
confirmed.claim: `from http.client import HTTPException` means every `raise HTTPException(status_code=..., detail=...)` in this router raises TypeError (http.client.HTTPException takes no keyword args) instead of a FastAPI HTTP error.
confirmed.trigger: Any code path that raises HTTPException: device-not-found (404) or not-an-SNMP-device/CCU (405) in reset_device and getlog.
confirmed.repro: GET /actions/getlog/9.9.9.9 for an IP not in the report -> get_device_by_ip returns None -> `raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...)` -> TypeError('HTTPException() takes no keyword arguments') -> FastAPI returns 500 instead of a clean 404. Verified: `from http.client import HTTPException; HTTPException(status_code=404, detail='x')` raises TypeError.

verdict.reasoning: Read actions.py:1-120. Line 5 is `from http.client import HTTPException` (fastapi is imported separately on line 8, but only for `APIRouter, Query, status` — NOT HTTPException). Every `raise HTTPException(status_code=..., detail=...)` in the file (lines 27-30, 36-39, 41-44 in reset_device; lines 59-62, 69-72 in getlog) passes keyword args to `http.client.HTTPException`, which takes none. I reproduced the failure statically: `python -c "from http.client import HTTPException; HTTPException(status_code=404, detail='x')"` -> `TypeError: HTTPException() takes no keyword arguments`. The trigger is reachable and unguarded: `get_device_by_ip` (cli/update.py:120-122) returns None via `next(..., None)` when the IP is absent from the report, so the None-check at line 58 fires the broken `raise` at line 59. In getlog there is NO try/except, so the TypeError propagates -> FastAPI returns 500 instead of a clean 404/405. In reset_device the body is wrapped in `try/except Exception` (lines 48-50), which swallows the TypeError and returns `{"success": False}` with HTTP 200 — masking the intended 404/405 entirely (an even worse error-masking outcome). No upstream guard prevents this; the bug is statically provable.
verdict.covered_by_test: none found — grep over tests/ for getlog|reset_device|HTTPException|actions returned zero matches; actions.py has no test coverage at all
verdict.blast_radius: Router-level, not vendor- or report-variant-specific: affects every /actions/getlog/{ip} and /actions/reset_device/{ip} call against any SNMP device on any consist (all 14 report variants). getlog leaks a 500 on device-not-found / non-SNMP / CCU; reset_device silently returns success:false. Any out-of-report or non-SNMP IP triggers it.

confirmed.title: reset_device masks 404/405 (and report-missing) as {success: False} HTTP 200
confirmed.claim: The bare `except Exception` in reset_device swallows the TypeError from the broken HTTPException raises AND the Exception thrown by get_devices when the report file is missing, returning {'success': False} with HTTP 200.
confirmed.trigger: Unknown IP, non-SNMP device, CCU device, or missing/unreadable report file.
confirmed.repro: GET /actions/reset_device/<ip-of-CCU> -> code intends 405 -> http.client.HTTPException(kwargs) -> TypeError -> caught by `except Exception` line 48 -> logged -> returns 200 {'success': False}. Caller cannot distinguish 'not found', 'wrong device type', and 'reboot actually failed'; all collapse to success:False/200.

verdict.reasoning:
Both legs of the claim are statically provable from the code I read.

(1) Wrong HTTPException import. actions.py line 5: `from http.client import HTTPException` — NOT fastapi's. http.client.HTTPException is `class HTTPException(Exception): pass` and takes no kwargs. I ran `HTTPException(status_code=404, detail='x')` and it raised `TypeError: HTTPException() takes no keyword arguments`. So the 404 raise (lines 27-30), the non-SNMP 405 raise (lines 36-39), and the CCU 405 raise (lines 41-44) each throw a TypeError, not an HTTP error.

(2) Missing report. reset_device line 25 calls get_device_by_ip(ip) → cli/update.py:121 get_devices(...) → line 71 `raise Exception(f"report file {report_file} does not exist")` when load_report returns None (file missing/unreadable; load_report swallows FileNotFoundError/PermissionError/JSONDecodeError → None at lines 36-47).

Both the TypeError and the bare Exception propagate into reset_device's `except Exception as e:` at line 48, which does `logger.error(e); return {"success": False}` (line 50). FastAPI serializes that dict with its default 200 status. So unknown IP, non-SNMP device, CCU device, and missing/unreadable report all collapse to {'success': False} HTTP 200 — indistinguishable from an actual reboot() returning False (line 46). Caller cannot tell apart not-found / wrong-type / no-report / real-failure.

Decisive corroboration: sibling router consist.py line 11 correctly imports `from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException`, and the intended contract is documented by green tests test_get_ip__not_found and test_get_mac__no_report (test_consist.py) which assert status_code==404 with a detail body for exactly the not-found and no-report cases. actions.py diverges by importing the wrong class and wrapping everything in a swallowing except.
verdict.covered_by_test: No test covers actions.py/reset_device (grep for 'reset_device|actions' in tests/ returns nothing). test_get_devices__does_not_exist (tests/cli/test_update.py:78) confirms get_devices raises Exception on a missing report. test_get_ip__not_found and test_get_mac__no_report (tests/lib/server/test_consist.py:58,42) assert the CORRECT 404+detail behavior for the sibling consist router — documenting the opposite of what actions.py does, reinforcing this is a defect not intent.
verdict.blast_radius: Not vendor- or report-variant-specific. Affects the /actions/reset_device/{ip} endpoint for every device type and every train/report variant: all 404 (unknown IP), all 405 (non-SNMP device, CCU device), and all missing/unreadable-report cases collapse to {'success': False} HTTP 200. The same wrong import also breaks getlog (lines 59/69), but getlog has no outer try/except so it 500s instead of masking — related, outside this claim's scope.

confirmed.title: togglepoe can deref parentSW.mac when cache supplies port but loop nulls parentSW
confirmed.claim: When port is seeded from the powered_down_aps cache but the neighbours loop runs and sets parentSW=None (no matching switch), `not port` is False so execution reaches line 112 `LldpWalker().instantiate_device(mac=parentSW.mac, ...)` -> AttributeError on None.
confirmed.trigger: ap_ip present in powered_down_aps cache (so port is truthy) AND the AP still reports neighbours but none of those neighbour IPs match a switch in the current report.
confirmed.repro: Power an AP off (cache stores (SW,port)), then before the AP drops its neighbour list, call togglepoe again with a report where the neighbour switch IP is absent -> loop sets parentSW=None, port stays truthy from cache -> `if not port` False -> parentSW.mac -> AttributeError -> 500.

verdict.reasoning: Read the full togglepoe handler at actions.py:83-119. The mechanism is statically airtight. Line 96 seeds both vars from the module-global cache: `parentSW, port = powered_down_aps.get(ap_ip, (None, None))`. The cache is only populated at line 118 (`powered_down_aps[ap_ip] = (parentSW, port)`) after a successful power-off where a matching switch existed, so the cached `port` is a real truthy value. The loop at 97-105 then runs over the CURRENT report's neighbours: line 98 `parentSW = next((x for x in switches if x.ip == neigh["ip"]), None)` UNCONDITIONALLY reassigns parentSW every iteration; line 99 `if parentSW:` only updates port/breaks on a match. So if the AP's current neighbours list is non-empty but none of those neigh["ip"] values match a switch in the current report, the loop exits with parentSW=None while port retains its truthy cached value (port is never touched on the no-match path). Line 109 `if not port:` is therefore False (port is truthy), execution falls through to line 112 `LldpWalker().instantiate_device(mac=parentSW.mac, ip=parentSW.ip)` -> AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'mac'. There is NO try/except in togglepoe (unlike reset_device at lines 23/48 which wraps its body), and no FastAPI exception_handler/middleware exists under lib/server (grep returned nothing), so the uncaught AttributeError yields HTTP 500 — exactly the claimed outcome. The hunter's logic and TRIGGER are correct.
verdict.covered_by_test: none found — grep for togglepoe/powered_down/set_port_poe across tests/ returned zero matches; the endpoint is entirely untested
verdict.blast_radius: Single API endpoint (/actions/togglepoe). Vendor-agnostic (any AP/SW in the report), NOT tied to the 14 report-generation variants — it is a PoE-toggle action, not report rendering. Triggers on any train where the PoE-off-then-toggle-again UI action runs against an AP whose cached (SW,port) entry exists but whose current report neighbours reference no in-report switch (e.g. report regenerated between calls, switch dropped/renamed, or stale LLDP). Impact is a 500 on that one action, not data corruption.

confirmed.title: getlog raises raw Exception (report missing) and broken HTTPException as 500
confirmed.claim: getlog has no try/except; get_device_by_ip -> get_devices raises Exception('report file ... does not exist') when load_report returns None, and the http.client HTTPException raises TypeError, both surfacing as unhandled 500s with internal detail.
confirmed.trigger: Report file missing/unreadable, or requested IP not found, or device not an SNMPDevice.
confirmed.repro: GET /actions/getlog/1.2.3.4 with no report file present -> get_devices (cli/update.py:71) raises Exception -> propagates uncaught from getlog -> 500 leaking 'report file <path> does not exist'.

verdict.reasoning: Both halves statically provable. (1) getlog (actions.py:53-80) has NO try/except — contrast reset_device (lines 23-50) which wraps everything in try/except and returns {"success": False}. getlog line 57 calls get_device_by_ip (cli/update.py:120-122), which calls get_devices(...), which at cli/update.py:65-71 does `if devices := load_report(report_file): ... else: raise Exception(f"report file {report_file} does not exist")`. load_report (update.py:34-47) returns None on FileNotFoundError/PermissionError/etc. So a missing/unreadable report makes get_devices raise a raw Exception that propagates uncaught out of getlog → FastAPI 500 leaking the internal report-file path. needs_runtime.title: needs_firmware_update None.endswith when firmware unread

needs_runtime.trigger: target contains a 'firmware' key but the live firmware read returned None (snmpdevice _snmp_get returns None on any SNMP error).

needs_runtime.title: Per-batch firmware-then-config both sleep 5 min; config update skipped if device IP changes after firmware reboot
needs_runtime.claim: update() processes firmware then config for the same batch assuming the device keeps its IP across the firmware reboot; the code's own comment admits no ARP/ping reacquisition, so a post-firmware IP change makes the subsequent config push hit a stale IP and silently fail (SNMPDeviceException swallowed in update_device).
needs_runtime.trigger: A device that changes IP after a firmware update is targeted with action 'fc'.
needs_runtime.repro: Run `obn update fc <ip>` on a device that DHCP-renews to a new IP after firmware reboot. Firmware batch reboots it; config batch (same Device.ip) talks to the old IP, set_configuration_version raises SNMPDeviceException, which update_device catches at line 211 and returns without surfacing failure -> config silently not applied.

verdict.reasoning: Static facts in cli/update.py confirm the structural claim. In update() the per-batch loop (lines 310-321) processes `batch & update_set.firmware_updates` via process_batch(union,"f"), sleeps 5*60, then processes `batch & update_set.config_updates` via process_batch(union,"c"), sleeps 5*60 — firmware then config for the SAME batch using the SAME Device objects, which carry the report-time device.ip. The code's own comment (lines 304-307) explicitly admits the gap: "we _assume_ that the device won't change IP address after the firmware update. If it does, we'll need to implement a technique (combination of ARP and ping) to reacquire the IP address to proceed with the configuration update." I confirmed no reacquisition exists on this path: update_device() -> get_snmpdevice(device) -> LldpWalker().instantiate_device(mac=device.mac, ip=device.ip) (update.py:143-144), and instantiate_device (walker.py:30-64) constructs the vendor class with the passed-in ip verbatim — it never calls ARPLookup/DHCPLookup.get_ip_from_mac to re-resolve. So a post-firmware IP change would make the config push hit the stale report-time IP, and set_configuration_version() raising SNMPDeviceException is caught at update.py:211-214 and the function returns. TWO caveats keep this from "confirmed": (1) the claim says config "silently" fails, but update_device does NOT fail silently — it calls logger.exception(...) and prints "error during configuration update" to stdout (lines 212-213), so the failure IS surfaced in logs/console, contradicting the "silently swallowed" framing. (2) The actual fault only manifests when a real device DHCP-renews to a different IP within the firmware-reboot window AND needs both f+c; whether that occurs depends on lease timing/hardware and cannot be proven statically. The design gap is real and self-documented; the failure realization is runtime-dependent.

refuted.title: TNG4500 neighbours() crashes when LLDP value is not parseable as MAC
refuted.claim: mac.rsplit(":",1) raises AttributeError because parse_mac_address(value) returns None for a non-6-byte value, and mac is used unguarded; the is_mac_address() validator defined at line 106 is never called.

refuted.repro: Call Table._validate({'ip':'10.x','firmware':None,'target':{'firmware':'v8'}}, 'firmware'): line 75 `'firmware' not in device` is False (key exists), line 89 `target in device['firmware']` -> `'v8' in None` -> TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable; even with empty target, line 92 `device['firmware'] + ' '` -> None + str TypeError. Crashes the whole `obn validate` table render.

verdict.reasoning: The cited code is real: backbone_validate.py:75 `if item not in device: return "incomplete"` only catches a MISSING key, and line 89 `valid = target in device[item]` plus line 92 `device[item] + " "` would both TypeError if device[item] were None. The hunter's reasoning about _validate in isolation is sound. HOWEVER the trigger is unreachable through OBN's actual data flow. (1) `obn validate` reads ONLY cfg.report_file (discovery.prev.json): load_devices() hardcodes `open(cfg.report_file)` (backbone_validate.py:132-137) and the CLI `validate` command (obn.py:104-108) exposes no input-file override. (2) discovery.prev.json is written solely by Report.store_report() -> dump_device_instances() -> Device.as_dict(skip_empty=True) (lib/report/report.py:137-141, lib/report/device.py:47-53), and that serializer DROPS every field whose value is None: `{k: v for k,v in self.__dict__.items() if not (skip_empty and (v is None or v == list()))}`. (3) A device whose SNMP firmware/config OID genuinely returned None — reachable: snmpdevice.firmware_version/configuration_version -> generic_get -> _snmp_get returns None at line 328 (empty OID) or line 340 (`result.get(oid)` miss on failed/empty get; empty strings are skipped at lines 303-304) — therefore lands in the REPORT with the firmware/config key OMITTED, not set to None. (4) When validate reads it back, line 75 `item not in device` is True -> returns "incomplete", and None never reaches line 89/92. The skip_empty serializer is the upstream guard that converts present-None into absent-key, which the line-75 guard already handles. The hunter's escape hatches don't hold: hand-edited JSON is out of scope (any field could be corrupted that way), and validate cannot be pointed at the raw output_file (discovery.json) that retains None. Note: discovery.py's own Device.as_dict (lib/device/device.py:12-21) DOES write present-None into discovery.json, but that file is never the input to validate.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/test_backbone_validate.py::TestTable::test_create_incomplete_switch_overview (with resources/test_backbone_validate/discovery_incomplete.json, where firmware/config keys are absent) green-asserts the "incomplete" path — the same outcome the skip_empty serializer guarantees for a None firmware/config. No test feeds a present-but-None firmware/config (test_validate__empty_firmware uses an empty TARGET, not a None device value), but none is needed because the report serializer makes present-None unreachable.
verdict.blast_radius: Would have spanned all SNMP devices (switches + APs) across all report variants in `obn validate`, since _validate runs on every firmware/config cell — but it is neutralized fleet-wide by the skip_empty serializer that produces discovery.prev.json. No vendor/report variant is actually exposed through the supported obn validate flow.

refuted.title: Table._validate crashes on null IP via ipaddress.ip_address(None)
refuted.claim: When a device dict carries ip=None, ipaddress.ip_address(device['ip']) raises and aborts the entire validate overview.
refuted.trigger: A discovered device with no resolvable IP is serialized with ip:null into the report (e.g. GenericDevice / DHCP-relay entry, or any device whose IP lookup returned None).
refuted.repro: Feed validate a device {'type':'SW','ip':None,'coach_number':1,'device_number':1}; _create_overview calls _validate(device,'ip'); 'ip' in device is True so line 83 runs ipaddress.ip_address(None) -> TypeError/ValueError, uncaught, aborting create_switch_overview for all devices, not just the bad one.

verdict.reasoning: Line 83 is real: `ip = ipaddress.ip_address(device["ip"])`. The upstream guard at line 75 (`if item not in device: return "incomplete ✗"`) only checks KEY PRESENCE, not None value, so a literal in-memory dict `{'ip': None}` passed straight to `_validate` would indeed reach line 83 and raise ValueError uncaught (the loop at lines 105-113 has no try/except). The hunter's unit-level repro is accurate AT THE FUNCTION LEVEL. BUT the stated TRIGGER ("serialized with ip:null into the report") is false for the file `validate` actually reads. `backbone_validate.load_devices` (lines 132-137) reads `cfg.report_file` = discovery.prev.json, which is written by lib/report/report.py:store_report (lines 137-141) -> dump_device_instances (line 50) -> lib/report/device.py:as_dict(skip_empty=True) (lines 47-53): `if not (skip_empty and (v is None or v == list()))` OMITS any None field. So a None IP serializes as an ABSENT "ip" key, NOT "ip": null. Against that report, line 75 catches it -> returns "incomplete ✗", line 83 never runs. Furthermore _create_overview filters on x["type"]=="SW" (line 103) and reads x["coach_number"]/x["device_number"] (lines 106-107) unguarded; a GenericDevice (the claim's cited source, lib/device/genericdevice.py ip=None default) has type/coach/device defaulting to None in the report-layer Device dataclass, which skip_empty also omits, so it never matches the type filter and is excluded before IP validation. The only as_dict that emits ip:null is the discovery-layer lib/device/device.py (line 13, unconditional), but that feeds discovery.json, which backbone_validate does NOT read. The trigger's factual premise is contradicted by the serializer on the actual read path.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/test_backbone_validate.py::TestTable::test_create_incomplete_switch_overview and test_validate__incomplete — both exercise the missing-field/"incomplete" path (resources/test_backbone_validate/discovery_incomplete.json has a VALID ip "10.171.100.41" and omits firmware/config keys), confirming the line-75 guard handles absent keys. No test feeds ip=None, but none is needed since the report serializer never produces a null ip.
verdict.blast_radius: Would be all 4 overview variants (SW/AP/ICL/MEDIA) across every consist if reachable, since _validate is shared. But unreachable via the report-file path on all of them because lib/report/device.py:as_dict(skip_empty=True) omits None ip before backbone_validate ever loads it. No customer report variant or SNMP device class produces a "ip": null entry in discovery.prev.json.

refuted.title: ZabbixGenerator.generate_nodes KeyErrors on missing coach_number
refuted.claim: generate_nodes indexes node['coach_number'] with [] rather than .get(), raising KeyError for any discovered node lacking the key.
refuted.trigger: discovery.prev.json contains a device entry without a 'coach_number' field (e.g. a comms-failed device recorded by backbone_discovery as just {'mac','ip'}, or a GenericDevice/unknown-prefix entry).
refuted.repro: backbone_discovery.discover() appends {'mac':..,'ip':..} (no coach_number) for devices whose SNMP uptime is None (line 82) or unknown MAC (line 70). Run `zabbix_generate.py` against that file: ZabbixGenerator.generate_nodes line 46 `node['coach_number']` -> KeyError, crashing Zabbix LLD generation. ZabbixChecker.check (line 95) guards with `all(key in device ...)` but generate_nodes does not.

verdict.reasoning: The cited line is real: lib/zabbix.py:46 reads `node["coach_number"]` with `[]`, not `.get()`, and unlike ZabbixChecker.check (line 95-96, guarded by `all(key in device ...)`) generate_nodes has no key guard. So in isolation it would KeyError on a coach_number-less record. BUT the hunter's TRIGGER is false. zabbix_generate.py:7-11 feeds DISCOVERY_PREV_JSON = "/tmp/discovery.prev.json" to ZabbixGenerator. That path is `Configuration.report_file` (configuration.py:80-82), NOT the raw backbone_discovery output. discovery.prev.json is written exclusively by Report.store_report() (report.py:137-141), which dumps self.device_instances. run_report() (report.py:623-624) calls number_coaches() before store_report(), and every one of the 14 concrete number_coaches implementations calls normalise_devices() (verified by grep: report_ace/ccjpa_wd1/ccjpa_wd2/daisy_cybox/dani/dhcp/dosto_neu/dsb/generic/luna/queensland/tgv/tgv2020/via). normalise_devices (report.py:253-260) explicitly removes every device where `v.coach_number is not None and v.device_number is not None and v.type is not None` is false — i.e. it strips exactly the comms-failed/{mac,ip}-only entries the hunter relies on. Belt-and-suspenders: store_report() sorts the dumped list with itemgetter("coach_number","device_number","type") at report.py:140 BEFORE writing, so a coach_number-less record could not even be serialized into the file. The raw discovery output the hunter describes (entries with only mac/ip) lives in the separate output_file (discovery.json), which ZabbixGenerator never opens. The hunter conflated discovery.json (raw, pre-normalisation) with discovery.prev.json (post-normalisation report snapshot). No production path can produce the triggering file shape, so the defect-as-described cannot fire.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/lib/test_zabbix.py::TestZabbix — test_all_present, test_physical_coach_numbers, test_one_switch_per_coach all feed generator.discovered_consist entries that uniformly include coach_number (the file's invariant) and assert the happy path; none feed a coach_number-less entry, matching the real input contract enforced by normalise_devices. No test contradicts the bug, but none can reach it either.
verdict.blast_radius: All 14 report variants share the same normalise_devices guard in number_coaches, so the protective invariant on discovery.prev.json holds fleet-wide (DOSTO and every other customer). Zabbix LLD generation is unaffected across the board. The only residual is a latent defensive-coding nit on zabbix.py:46 that is not reachable via any current writer of discovery.prev.json.

refuted.title: get_walker returns None for unrecognized walker_type -> None.walk()
refuted.claim: get_walker has no else branch, so any walker_type value other than the three hardcoded strings returns None, and discover() then calls None.walk().
refuted.trigger: A report module defines a walker_type attribute that is a string not in {'LldpWalker','LldpArpWalker','DhcpWalker'} (e.g. a renamed/new walker), or returns an unexpected value.
refuted.repro: Set report_module to a reporter whose walker_type='SomeNewWalker'; get_walker (lines 33-38) matches no branch and falls off the function returning None; discover() line 49 `for dev in wlk.walk():` -> AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'walk'.

verdict.reasoning: The hunter is right that get_walker (backbone_discovery.py:30-38) has no else branch and would implicitly return None for a walker_type string outside {"LldpWalker","LldpArpWalker","DhcpWalker"}. But the falsifiable claim and its TRIGGER ("a report module defines walker_type as a string not in the three names") describe data that does not exist anywhere in the tree. I enumerated every source of walker_type: (1) get_walker_type line 26 `walker_type = getattr(reporter, "walker_type", "LldpWalker".__str__)` falls back to the string "LldpWalker"; (2) grep for `walker_type` across lib/report shows ONLY two definitions — report_dhcp.py:8 returns "DhcpWalker" and report_via.py:10 returns "LldpArpWalker"; (3) the base Report class (report.py) defines no walker_type, so all other report classes inherit nothing and hit the fallback "LldpWalker". Thus the only three reachable values are exactly the three handled branches. The separate None case the hunter conflated into the trigger is explicitly guarded upstream at lines 31-32: `if (walker_type := get_walker_type(cfg)) is None: return LldpWalker()`. To make get_walker fall off and return None you would have to ADD a new report whose walker_type returns a novel string — a hypothetical future edit, not a live defect. Statically, the bug is unreachable.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/test_backbone_discovery.py::test_get_walker__unknown_module (report_module="UnknownReport" -> getattr returns None -> fallback "LldpWalker" -> asserts isinstance(walker, LldpWalker)); plus test_get_walker__lldp_arp_walker, test_get_walker__default_lldp_walker, test_get_walker__default_dhcp_walker, test_get_walker_type__default, test_get_walker_type__via_report — all six exercise the function and assert a concrete walker, never None.
verdict.blast_radius: None in practice. All 16 report modules resolve to one of the three handled walker types (14 inherit the "LldpWalker" fallback, report_dhcp -> DhcpWalker, report_via -> LldpArpWalker). The missing else is a latent defensive gap that only a future broken/renamed report could trip; no current report variant or device path reaches it.
